question: Does fixing the known true Vs and density isolate more interpretable Vp sensitivity in the existing P-SV examples?
hypothesis_not_result: Removing Vs mismatch may clarify Vp gradients; no improvement or thin-bed recovery is assumed before the new runs.

intervention.density: known constant2450kg/m3 in both truth and initial
intervention.target: all true fields with the existing constant-density convention

numerics.route: new native forward, new residual, data-only AD VJP, new adjoint; no old-gradient selection
numerics.gate: existing declared relative tolerances retained; any failure stays in its own namespace
numerics.physical_materials: finite positive rho, positive solid mu and bulk; known acoustic water separately; negative lambda disclosed if present
numerics.resources: hpnewpc3-via-vps: native MPI2 max, GPU idle only, nice10 and BLAS/Torch1; no other jobs stopped

panel_roles.fixed_vs: known structural prior, not an inverted result
panel_roles.delta_vp: input correction, explicitly not a gradient

comparison: Old/new Vp gradients in their original coordinates; same raw-display rule; no amplitude score where objectives or scales differ; AD/H share scales.
integrity: No gradient smoothing, gain, sharpening, added true texture or unreported data selection. Full gradients retained; any display saturation and data-proof sampling disclosed.
scope: A controlled known-Vs single-gradient experiment, not a full inversion or blind multiparameter reconstruction.
exports: PNG300dpi and editable PDF/SVG; report-sized, final glyph>=5pt; alignment1.5pt, final-PDF collision checks and every-panel inspection.
